questions.question: Which task belongs to the Transport Officer?
options: C. Assigning destination hospitals and logging each departure
D. Setting up red/yellow/green treatment zones
questions.rationale: Transport matches patients to vehicles and hospitals and tracks them.

questions.question: The Triage Officer encounters a patient with arterial bleeding from the thigh. They should:
options: B. Apply a tourniquet, tag, and move on
questions.rationale: Hemorrhage control is a seconds-long LSI permitted during triage.

questions.question: Where should ambulances wait until called?
questions.rationale: Staging keeps uncommitted units organized and out of the scene until the Transport Officer requests them.

questions.question: Who sets up the red/yellow/green zones of the treatment area?
questions.rationale: The Treatment Officer establishes and runs the treatment area.

questions.question: The best way for hospitals to receive MCI information is:
options: A. Each ambulance calls its own destination
B. A single Medical Communications Coordinator / hospital coordination point
questions.rationale: One voice prevents duplicate calls and gives an accurate picture of distribution.

questions.question: A crew arrives and asks staging 'Can we just go grab a patient?' The correct reply is:
options: B. No — wait with the vehicle until the Transport Officer calls you to the loading zone
D. Go to the command post

questions.question: Dead victims at an MCI should generally be:
options: A. Left in place unless blocking access to the living
B. Moved immediately to the treatment area
D. Covered and put in an ambulance
questions.rationale: Leave in place: preserves resources, the scene, and identification.

questions.question: Which is NOT a role of the EMS Incident Commander?
options: A. Assigning triage and transport officers
B. Coordinating with police and fire
D. Inserting an advanced airway on a red patient
questions.rationale: The IC does not provide hands-on care.

questions.question: The treatment area is full and nothing is leaving. The MOST likely failure is in:
questions.rationale: Treatment areas back up when transport and staging aren't moving vehicles efficiently.

questions.question: A transport log primarily ensures:
options: A. Every patient can be located — which unit took them and to which hospital
questions.rationale: Tracking reunites families, informs hospitals, and supports re-triage and accountability.
